proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the finite-sample estimation and uniformly honest expected-length rate frontier for the known power-law oracle transport experiment, and the mathematical referee passed with no findings. The field-tier novelty gate stopped the run at subfield: exact known weights, no sampled-target or weight-estimation uncertainty, and stylized tail geometry limited the package to a benchmark. The two bank-positioning findings remain unrepaired; a field-tier continuation requires a new load-bearing theorem package, not a citation-only revision.
tldr: In a randomized source encouragement trial linked to a target population through target monotonicity and two target-averaged direct mean-transport restrictions, a known power-law target density can concentrate enough mass near source-rare covariates to make the transported score have infinite variance while target compliance may vanish. Source exclusion remains necessary for the observed reduced form, but neither source monotonicity nor target exclusion defines the headline class, and target and source conditional mediated contrasts may differ across \(X\). Over the class specified only by the disclosed lower bound \(\mu_n(P_n)\ge a_n\), minimax absolute error and minimax uniformly honest expected length both have order \(\min\{1,n^{-(1-\rho)}/a_n\}\). A clipped encouragement score controls the original causal Wald ratio through an explicit deterministic bias envelope, and affine inversion remains valid even with zero score variance or a zero empirical denominator. A lawful least-favorable continuum at first stage \(3a_n/2\) uses a copied conditional kernel only as a convenient stronger witness, lies in the source-monotone and target-exclusion subclass, and gives the matching full-observation converse. A separately constructed no-shift benchmark has zero clipping bias and class-level information scale \(na_n^2/\kappa_n\), in contrast to the power-law scale \(n^{2(1-\rho)}a_n^2\).
gap: Transported-CACE theory gives identification and regular Gaussian inference, heavy-tail weighting theory gives truncation rates for means or policy values, and weak-IV theory gives score inversion. None of the located results characterizes their joint minimax error and honest-length frontier when the known transport weight is not square integrable and target compliance shrinks.
fill: The project pairs an implementable finite-sample interval and projected-denominator estimator with a same-class rare-region continuum lower experiment, proving the polynomial phase transition for both point estimation and arbitrary measurable confidence sets and contrasting it with a directly constructed finite-Kish root-\(n\) reduction.
